CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Roberts is a 49-year-old male with a long-standing history of hypertension since young age. He recently presented to the emergency room with elevated blood pressure and palpitations in March. He attributes this episode to consuming a few cups of coffee without breakfast and reports it may have been a panic attack. He denies recurrence of palpitations since that time. He was started on a new medication (Benicar HCT 40-25) approximately one month ago by his new primary care physician. He continues to take amlodipine 10 mg daily. He monitors his blood pressure at home every morning and reports readings in the range of 146-155 mmHg. He is attempting to reduce his salt intake and exercises by walking on the treadmill when he can.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Benicar HCT (40-25 containing hydrochlorothiazide).
Amlodipine 10 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Significant family history of hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with girlfriend. Exercises on treadmill when able.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs: Clear to auscultation. Abdomen: Soft, no areas of tenderness with palpation. Extremities: No swelling noted in ankles and feet.

RESULTS
Potassium one week ago: 4.0.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Resistant hypertension on three medications at maximum dose. Patient was counseled that he meets criteria for resistant hypertension. Spironolactone has been added to his medication regimen. Potential side effects discussed include dizziness, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance (hyperkalemia and hyponatremia), and gynecomastia (rare, approximately 1 in 100 males). Patient counseled on lifestyle modifications including DASH diet, salt restriction to less than 2000 mg daily (ideally 1500 mg daily), increasing potassium intake, and regular aerobic exercise for 30 minutes most days to help lower blood pressure. Patient provided with information on DASH eating plan and directed to heart.org for additional resources. Follow-up appointment scheduled in two weeks for blood pressure check and metabolic panel to monitor potassium and sodium levels. If resistant hypertension persists on spironolactone, patient will be referred to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of procedural interventions such as renal denervation.
